clue.text: Is tale about a champion of the court?

indicators.note: 'about' as in turned about: the preceding words are read from the back

parts.note: a saga is a long tale

explanation.surface: A question whether some story concerns a tennis star.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words together are turned round, not each one separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi won eight Grand Slam singles titles on the tennis court.

clue.text: Eventer, girl rode, bothered dog

indicators.note: something bothered is ruffled and disturbed, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An eventing horse, ridden by a girl, was upset by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: An eventer is a horse that competes in eventing; the horse-riding picture hides that the three words are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden retriever is a popular breed of gun dog with a yellow coat.

clue.text: Man's on air, being broadcast in republic

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man is on the radio, transmitted in some republic.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Bury at home getting fright? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half the word survives, the rest being cut away

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether burying a person at home causes alarm, and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it keeps only the first half of the fright word.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a corpse in a grave, a formal synonym.

clue.text: More than one mall has cedars spreading round centre of plaza

indicators.note: round means placed around something else, enclosing it
spreading suggests things moving apart and settling in new places
the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

explanation.surface: A shopping centre has cedar trees spread around the middle of its square.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcades are covered shopping passages, so the plural is several malls.

clue.text: Disclosure made by a daughter on crusade

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a crusade is a campaign or mission pursued with zeal

explanation.surface: A revelation made by a young woman while campaigning for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Confessing or owning up to something is a disclosure of it.

clue.text: Georgia caught leg earlier leaving dance

indicators.note: earlier means placed before, so the pieces named first go at the front ahead of the state

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A woman called Georgia, having hurt her leg earlier, quits the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' tells you the caught and leg pieces come before Georgia's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance done in a long single-file line.

clue.text: Located European, reportedly a threat to the king

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard by word of mouth, so a word is wanted by its sound

parts.note: a Czech is a European, and the spelling is swapped for its twin in sound

explanation.surface: A European has been found and is said to endanger the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is the chess piece, not a real monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a discovered check attacks the king when a piece moves out of the way of another.

clue.text: Poet may be modest about magazine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

explanation.surface: Perhaps a poet is bashful about appearing in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: It's ages since we met, so let me in on e.g. changes

indicators.note: changes indicates the letters before it are altered into a new order

parts.words: so let me in on e.g.

explanation.surface: A greeting to an old friend asking to be let in on the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to the comma; everything after it, including 'so', is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a casual greeting to someone not seen for a long while.

clue.text: Article one came across after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A news item where someone was encountered after an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or thing in a list or collection.

clue.text: Reference book he's got in house

indicators.note: got in means placed inside something else

parts.note: in astrology a sign of the zodiac is a house; Taurus is one

explanation.surface: Someone owns a reference book at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a home, but it means an astrological house.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing synonyms.

clue.text: A ring forming a reef

parts.note: to toll is to ring, as a bell does

explanation.surface: Something circular makes up a reef, as an atoll does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a noun describing the reef's shape, but it is the verb used of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Injured? One inside must be joined

indicators.note: inside means put within another word

explanation.surface: Someone hurt asks whether someone inside must be connected.
explanation.definitionFit: Married means joined in wedlock, or more generally united.

clue.text: Appraised newly-constructed exit

definitions.note: a verb: to go out of sight or leave

indicators.note: something newly constructed is built afresh from the same materials, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surveyor has valued a newly built way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exit' reads as a noun, a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave, and to disappear is to go out of view.

clue.text: Irreligion shown by warriors yet to be converted

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Lack of faith among fighters who have not yet been converted to a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu army unit, a word crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiety is a lack of reverence for God, close to irreligion.

clue.text: Employees in Nelson upset after rep knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word is read backwards
upset means disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Staff at a place called Nelson are distressed after a sales rep is run down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the turned rep first, before the rearranged name.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: Pantomime character, object of ridicule — ugly son?

parts.note: the butt of a joke is its target

indicators.note: something made ugly is disfigured, so its letters are misshapen into a new order

explanation.surface: A panto figure, mocked and asked whether he is the ugly son.
explanation.walkthrough: In the pantomime Cinderella, Buttons is the page boy, mocked alongside the Ugly Sisters; a pantomime is a British Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is the stock comic servant in the British Cinderella pantomime.

clue.text: Crew made out cutter

parts.note: a band is a group or crew
to make out something is to see it

explanation.surface: A gang has managed to cut something out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsaw is a power tool with a looped blade used for cutting.

clue.text: Kids' playroom has railway laid by carer

indicators.note: laid by means set down next to, so one piece sits directly after the other

parts.note: RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A children's room has a toy railway set up by the child-minder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid by' places the railway beside the carer, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a room in a house set aside for young children.

clue.text: House in Tipperary or Kilkenny

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the next few words

parts.note: the end of the first name, the middle word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A house is located in one of two Irish counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipperary and Kilkenny are counties in Ireland; 'House' means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of York was an English royal dynasty in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Diana disguised as a water nymph

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana dresses up as a water spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a nymph living in a spring, river or lake.

clue.text: Capital husband invested in food shop

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, like money put into a business

explanation.surface: A husband put money into a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money for investing, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, as New Delhi, is the capital territory of India.

clue.text: Vehicle part Carol damaged

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Carol has dented part of her car.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol car is a police vehicle used to patrol an area.

clue.text: Ring-shaped object, disc with awful rust round it

indicators.note: round it means wrapped around the earlier piece
awful means very bad, so the letters are in a mess

explanation.surface: A doughnut-shaped part, a disc covered in nasty corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a torus is a doughnut-like ring surface.

clue.text: Son phoned about bad sign linked to English fruit

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first pair encloses the next words

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A son rang about a bad omen connected to some English fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The son and phoned pieces together surround bad and sign; English is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Seville orange is a bitter orange used for marmalade.

clue.text: Fighting man arrives in West Indies ahead of certain soldiers

indicators.note: ahead of means placed in front of what follows
in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: standard abbreviation for the West Indies
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A soldier lands in the Caribbean before his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior is a brave or experienced fighter.

clue.text: Dog from UK in a short list, possibly

indicators.note: in means placed inside the letters that follow
possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters, not the given one
short means cut off, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A dog from Britain may appear on a shortlist.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender hunting hound breed from the Middle East.
